items.name: Feastables
clues: January 2022.
A snack brand from the most-subscribed YouTuber in the world.
He hid golden tickets in the bars, like in “Charlie and the Chocolate Factory”, and the winners competed in a video for a Wonka-style chocolate factory.
Chocolate bars at first, later cookies and gummy sweets, now in big supermarkets, including in Germany.
Jimmy Donaldson, from North Carolina, famous for enormous challenges and giving away money.
A big celebration meal, turned into a word for things you can eat with “-ables” at the end.

items.name: Air Jordan
clues: 1985, in the United States.
A sports company bet a huge amount of money on a rookie basketball player and gave him his own shoe.
The story of how the deal happened became a 2023 film starring Matt Damon and Ben Affleck.
Mostly trainers, re-released again and again in new colours. Collectors know them by numbers, like the 1, the 4 or the 11, and by a logo of a player flying towards the basket.
He won six titles with the Chicago Bulls in the 1990s.
The name of the sports company's cushioning technology, plus the player's surname.

items.name: Prime
clues: January 2022.
A drink from two YouTubers who used to be rivals and once fought each other in a boxing ring.
In December 2022, British teenagers queued and pushed to get bottles when a supermarket chain started selling it, and some shops resold it for many times the price.
Sports drinks and energy drinks in very colourful bottles and cans.
An American wrestler and podcaster, and a British rapper who started out making football video game videos.
A word meaning “the best possible time or condition”, as in “in the ___ of life”.

items.name: Rhode
clues: June 2022, sold only on its own website at first.
Just three products at the start: a lip treatment, a “glazing” serum and a cream.
In 2025 the beauty company e.l.f. agreed to buy it for up to $1 billion, about three years after it launched.
Skincare and make-up in calm, pale packaging, for the shiny look its founder called “glazed donut skin”.
A model who is married to a Canadian pop star.
Her middle name, which is also the name of a Greek island without its last letter.

items.name: Haus Labs
clues: September 2019.
A make-up line that was sold only on Amazon at first.
In 2022 it relaunched with new “clean” formulas, and made its name a little shorter.
Lip glosses, eyeliners, and a foundation that launched with 51 shades.
A singer and actress who won an Oscar for a song from “A Star Is Born”.
The German word for “house”, plus a short word for laboratories.

items.name: Aviation Gin
clues: Portland, Oregon, 2006.
A small craft distillery's drink. A Hollywood star bought a share of it in 2018.
In 2020 the drinks giant Diageo agreed to buy it for up to $610 million.
Gin, sold with short, silly adverts starring its famous owner.
The actor who plays Deadpool and co-owns Wrexham football club.
The word for flying planes, which is also the name of a classic gin cocktail, plus the drink itself.
